video_title: Lakers Q&A: Luka’s Slovenia Vlog, Starting Competition, Media Day & More

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's leadership during the Slovenia team trip
quotes.excerpt: This entire trip was an awesome show of leadership from Luka to organize the trip.
quotes.quote: This entire trip was an awesome show of leadership from Luka to organize the trip, to fly the guys out there, and to have a variety of team-bonding activities. They played basketball, but they also golfed, they went rowing, they were racing bikes down the street, they were checking out castles. It is one thing to say you are going to step up as a leader or to go into the season hoping to step up as a leader, hoping to replace the void of losing LeBron James and Jarred Vanderbilt from a vocal leadership perspective, but Luka actually took action here, and that is commendable.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jarred Vanderbilt and Colin Sexton as the team's vibe curators
quotes.excerpt: Jarred Vanderbilt and Colin Sexton were the two MVPs. They were the vibe curators.
quotes.quote: Jarred Vanderbilt and Colin Sexton were the two MVPs. They were the vibe curators. Vando, you could just tell why he is so beloved by the group, constantly cracking jokes with the quips and always great vibes with Vando. Colin Sexton assimilated very well on the first group trip and had a similar vibe. I thought those two were really important for a group that can be a bit introverted. It is not the loudest group, it is not the most extroverted group, but when they are around each other, that can bring guys out of their shell.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Mamu's role in the Lakers' pick-and-roll defensive schemes
quotes.excerpt: They had Mamu showing high on a couple of the pick-and-roll clips and also switching.
quotes.quote: They had Mamu showing high on a couple of the pick-and-roll clips and also switching. It looks like while they might shift to drop with Walker Kessler, with Mamu, we saw a couple of possessions with Luka and Walker Kessler running pick-and-roll and Mamu was playing up to the touch and switching. Then, Colin Sexton called out a red, which is a switch, and then he switched on to Luka. But we then saw no low-man rotation and Walker Kessler got a wide-open dunk. So, the Lakers are going to have to work on their pick-and-roll defense.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential starting lineup featuring Quinton Grimes and Ziaire Williams
quotes.excerpt: It is easy to see LA potentially swapping Connect out, putting Austin Reaves in there.
quotes.quote: It is easy to see LA potentially swapping Dalton Knecht out, putting Austin Reaves in there, and then that starting group making a ton of sense with Quinton Grimes and Ziaire Williams, which would currently be my pick for who should be the five starters together. I think that makes a ton of sense on both sides of the ball.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Grading the Lakers' offseason moves and roster construction
quotes.excerpt: I am probably at a B. I think it is difficult to grade this offseason.
quotes.quote: I am probably at a B. I think it is difficult to grade this offseason, but one thing with offseason grades or with trade grades is you can have your perception of the move in the moment and then that is going to change with more time and seeing how things play out. If Walker Kessler does not pan out the way the Lakers expect him to pan out and they made the wrong move there, that is going to drop the grade. If Quinton Grimes or Mamu is like this massive hit on their contract, plus some of the minimum guys give them some real value and production in Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, etc., that would probably bump things up to a B+ or A- for me.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the value of the Cameron Carr trade
quotes.excerpt: Trading up for Cameron Carr and landing him at 24 was a steal.
quotes.quote: I think Cameron Carr, trading up for him and landing him at 24 was a steal. And I see the vision with Quinton Grimes, Mamu, and Ziaire Williams in terms of the upgrades over their predecessors in their processing and maybe their quicker decision-making in terms of shooting, moving the ball, attacking a closeout. I think there is a collective upgrade there.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' need for a backup center and starting-level wing
quotes.excerpt: I think they have four starting-caliber players and they still need a fifth one.
quotes.quote: I think they have four starting-caliber players and they still need a fifth one that I had hoped they were going to address or get that previously it was Kuminga, but get that starting four or starting wing that I think they clearly need. That upgrade over Ziaire Williams or Jake LaRavia. So, I think they have two pretty big holes in terms of a fifth starting-level player and like a backup five.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential for Adou to become a hybrid player
quotes.excerpt: I reckon he can be a DJ / Lu Dort hybrid.
quotes.quote: I like that. That is an interesting comparison. I think that is more in line with a realistic comparison for Adou. People have thrown out OG Anunoby and I just think that is a very high bar. OG Anunoby to me is an All-Star level player and was at times New York's second or even best player at various points of the postseason. He is one of the best two-way players in the league. If we are truly judging what you bring on both sides of the ball, I think OG Anunoby is in that conversation. So, the OG comparison, I see the frame, I see the outline of it to a degree with Adou, but I think that is a bit optimistic and generous.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Pairing Adou and Mamu in bench lineups
quotes.excerpt: I really like the idea of Adou and Mamu paired up in a four-five combination.
quotes.quote: I really like the idea of Adou and Mamu paired up in a four-five combination off of the bench where you have Adou as the primary screener and roller, rim runner, that vertical threat similar to a DJ, and he could do that as a roller. He could also do that cutting along the baseline or cutting from the dunker spot. And then Mamu being the guy who is around the elbow at the top of the arc, DHO guy, catch-and-shoot guy, pick-and-pop guy, and that inside-outside balance between Adou and Mamu. And then defensively, having Mamu be more of the four and Adou being more of the five, you could also do that with him being more of a natural rim protector and defensive anchor and interior defender compared to Mamu.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Expectations for Walker Kessler's performance this season
quotes.excerpt: A good goal for Kessler would be 65 plus games.
quotes.quote: A good goal for Kessler would be 65 plus games. If he plays at least 65, I think that is a nice start to his Lakers tenure. But more specifically, for me, a successful Kessler season would be 14-15 points, 11-12 rebounds, two plus blocks, being among the league leaders in field goal percentage. Those are some of the things I would throw out there in terms of benchmarks for Kessler. But I would like to see LA be at least a top-12 defense with Kessler on the floor and I would like to see a real impact on the offensive and defensive glass with him on the floor.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' defensive rating with Walker Kessler on the floor
quotes.excerpt: I would like to see LA be at least a top-12 defense with Kessler on the floor.
quotes.quote: I would like to see LA be at least a top-12 defense with Kessler on the floor and I would like to see a real impact on the offensive and defensive glass with him on the floor. And I think if he does, because we know he is going to run pick-and-rolls with Luka and Austin, he is going to be fed lobs and dump-off passes. I am not concerned with that. He is going to get his 10-12-14 points, he is going to get his 10-11-12 rebounds, he is going to get a couple blocks. The production, I think does need to be at a certain level, but I am fairly confident he is going to put up the numbers.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the Lu Dort trade on the Lakers' salary cap
quotes.excerpt: Because of the Lu Dort trade, the Hawks could not pay Jonathan Kuminga.
quotes.quote: Because of the Lu Dort trade, the Hawks could not pay Jonathan Kuminga, I believe it was like 11.3 million dollars, more than that. And the reason that is important is because to do a sign-and-trade, it has to be a legal signing for the team doing the sign-and-trade. So, the reason for that is like you cannot just be a team that signs a bunch of players, you are retaining the cap holds, and then is doing like an illegal move to go over the second apron or maybe you are past the second apron, and you are benefiting from, you know, maybe you are getting a pick or something for flipping a player when it is not really a legal move. So, to do a sign-and-trade, even as the team sending out the player, it has to be a legal move.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's decision to turn down the contract offer
quotes.excerpt: He clearly is betting on himself, he thinks very highly of himself, he believes in himself.
quotes.quote: He clearly is betting on himself, he thinks very highly of himself, he believes in himself. And to him, it did not make sense to commit to that type of contract long-term. He is hoping that he has a good season for the Wolves, they go on a deep playoff run, he shows he can be a part of winning basketball, and then he cashes out next summer with at least the non-taxpayer MLE if not potentially more.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The complexity of the sign-and-trade process for Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: It just got too complicated. The Lakers and the Hawks could not figure it out.
quotes.quote: It just got too complicated. The Lakers and the Hawks could not figure it out, the Lakers and Kuminga could not figure it out, and ultimately he did turn down something in this ballpark. It just was not for him, it did not make sense to commit to that type of contract long-term.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential for Kaluma to earn rotation minutes
quotes.excerpt: I think it is going to be predicated on him shooting the ball at a certain level.
quotes.quote: I think it is going to be predicated on him shooting the ball at a certain level because I mentioned this on yesterday's show, but I think you have to compare players, or the pathway for a guy like Kaluma to get into the rotation is by doing something that other guys cannot do. So, there is like the basic, he has to defend at a certain level and to me he does project more like a tweener of he is not really a three, he is not really a four, I am not really sure what his best position is defensively.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's playmaking and the need for high-level decision-makers
quotes.excerpt: What the Lakers are looking for is higher-level decision-makers in terms of the pass-dribble-shoot element.
quotes.quote: What the Lakers are looking for is higher-level decision-makers in terms of the pass-dribble-shoot element on the weak side. And so what I mean by that is if you think about some of the worst performances of the season from the Lakers, depending on the matchup, like Luka really struggled with OKC, Austin had his struggles with some of the top teams, LeBron had some rough games, but it to me it was not so much the stars, although again depending on the matchup, depending on the night, sometimes it was the stars, but oftentimes it would be the supporting cast going cold, then they start passing up shots, or they start rushing shots, or now they start doing too much off the dribble and they're dribbling the ball into traffic and trying to make certain passes or getting stripped or whatever.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' need for better perimeter defenders and playmakers
quotes.excerpt: The final guy needs to be able to guard on the wing but also guard some bigger forwards.
quotes.quote: The final guy needs to be able to guard on the wing but also guard some bigger forwards and that is where to be honest, I do not think Mamu could do either of those. But at least at a starting level, right? Like he could do it in a bench context, he cannot do it at a starting level in my opinion. But like he definitely I think can guard up better than he guards down. So, that that's like I I I think looking at this in a vacuum of what's the way to optimize Mamu, I don't even disagree with this assessment where I will push back is I don't think this is factoring in what's also best for Luka.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's passing ability and the team's offensive structure
quotes.excerpt: Luka was still one of the ten best passers in the NBA, if not arguably top five.
quotes.quote: Luka was still one of the ten best passers in the NBA, if not arguably top five. And you know, historically he is top ten, top five, whatever. But like even now, I think he was still in that conversation. And losing that is a massive blow. Like to me, he was the second best passer on this team behind Luka, higher level than Austin, and and that that's a real blow to the offense. So, they're going to have to figure out how to replace that, but I don't think the offense is going to change so much in how like in so far as how it looks. I think it's more so going to change in terms of the supporting cast going cold, then they start passing up shots, or they start rushing shots, or now they start doing too much off the dribble.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' strategy for building the roster around their stars
quotes.excerpt: I think the Lakers bet that they're trying to make is guys like Grimes and Sexton.
quotes.quote: I think the Lakers bet that they're trying to make is guys like Grimes and Sexton are objectively better drivers than Marcus Smart and Luke Kennard. Those guys can do other things better than them, right? Like I think Marcus is the best defender of the group and overall the highest basketball IQ. I think Luke is the best shooter of the group, even if he can be a reluctant shooter. And I think he's also an underrated driver and passer, but Colin Sexton is one of the better driving guards in the league, statistically. And Quinton Grimes also has the athleticism to attack a closeout and dunk on your head or or make a reverse layup or pull up for a mid-range jumper.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's ball-dominant style and the Lakers' roster adjustments
quotes.excerpt: I think it's more so that fine-tuning offensively, rather than an overhaul, if that makes sense.
quotes.quote: I think Luka is too ball-dominant to play a pass, dribble and shoot playstyle. Luka plays his best with high-level athletic defenders who can shoot threes at a high level. I think they have more confidence that the players they are replacing those guys with are just higher-level decision-makers who can do more with the ball in their hands. It's more so that fine-tuning offensively, rather than an overhaul, if that makes sense.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers have underachieved offensively during the Luka Doncic era
quotes.excerpt: I think the Lakers have underachieved offensively the last year and a half with Luka.
quotes.quote: I think there are ways to make the Lakers' offense more dynamic because if we're being truthful here, I think the Lakers have underachieved offensively the last year and a half with Luka. That's not all on Luka, but that's also not at all on Luka. It's partly on Luka, it's partly on JJ, it's partly on health, it's partly on Austin, it's partly on LeBron, it's partly on the collective. But certainly, I think there are things they could do offensively to go to a different level.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers did not strongly pursue LeBron James in free agency
quotes.excerpt: I don't think the Lakers really pursued him. And this is something that Pete has talked about.
quotes.quote: I think LeBron told the Lakers 'see ya', but there's a big caveat here because I don't think the Lakers really pursued him. And this is something that Pete has talked about a lot on his show and a bit on Lakers Collective in terms of a lot of the framing when we were talking about the Lakers and LeBron was through the LeBron lens and the clutch lens and not so much the Lakers lens. There were some public comments from Rob over the past year in terms of wanting to retain LeBron, wanting LeBron to retire a Laker, but I think we were more so assuming the Lakers wanted LeBron back rather than the reality being them not strongly pursuing him.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Westbrook trade created an irreparable fracture between the Lakers and LeBron
quotes.excerpt: I think the real end was the Westbrook trade and that created an irreparable fracture.
quotes.quote: I think the real end was the Westbrook trade and that created an irreparable fracture between the two sides that the Lakers stop consulting LeBron as much and asking for his input on the roster. LeBron, I think, grew a little colder toward the franchise and some of the primary decision-makers and ultimately, I think it was inevitable that they were going to part ways prematurely.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the potential of a Lakers roster featuring LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: If you took Kevon Looney from this roster and gave that spot to LeBron, I think this group would have a pretty high ceiling.
quotes.quote: If you took Kevon Looney from this roster and gave that spot to LeBron, I think this group would have a pretty high ceiling. I think it's difficult to make the case that they have a lower ceiling with LeBron in my opinion. I mean, I guess you could say defensively, and he was no longer the same shooter that he was as recently as a couple of years ago, but with what we saw from him last season, particularly in the playoffs, I think it's really difficult to make a case that the Lakers would somehow be worse with LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' decision to not re-sign DeAndre Ayton and trade Marcus Williams
quotes.excerpt: Rob has now made a couple of big calls on rescinding the Marcus Williams trade and passing on re-signing DeAndre Ayton.
quotes.quote: Rob has now made a couple of big calls on rescinding the Marcus Williams trade and passing on re-signing DeAndre Ayton, and both of them have worked out in terms of the medicals and those decisions. So I think he does deserve the benefit of the doubt in that regard. But Marcus was so important to this group and I would have felt better about the roster obviously if he was on the team, especially if he was in lieu of Quentin Grimes. But, you know, there have been some good things and now, of course, like Luka is involved with this with his recruiting and JJ recruiting and so it's not all on Rob and he, you know, he's the final decision-maker, but he's not the sole decision-maker.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: J.J. Redick is clearly the coach of the future for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: JJ clearly is like the coach of the future and is probably in better standing.
quotes.quote: Between the two, I think JJ clearly is like the coach of the future and is probably in better standing, where, you know, I think Rob, when there's an ownership change, like with him being such a senior executive, he's got to, of course, ingratiate himself with the new ownership group. JJ does too, but I think it's a little different where there's more player input on JJ and as long as Luka and Austin love JJ, I don't think JJ is going anywhere.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing the playmaking abilities of Quentin Grimes and Marcus Smart
quotes.excerpt: If you look at it exclusively through the passing lines, I would give the edge to Smart.
quotes.quote: If you look at it exclusively through the passing lines, I would give the edge to Smart. If you balance it with some of the scoring as well, I would maybe tilt it to Grimes. I think Grimes' scoring and shot creation, the gap there between the two might be higher in that regard than the passing. But there is a gap in my opinion between the passing. Like Grimes to me, he can rack up assists, he can get three, four, five assists, but he is more of a simple read guy in my opinion. It's like, I drive, I see the lob, I throw it, or I see the dump-off pass, I throw it, I see the kick-out pass, I throw it. The like second or third level of the playmaking, reading the floor, I don't see as much from him.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: J.J. Redick's blunt assessment of Cam Carr's need to gain weight
quotes.excerpt: JJ made a point to say that Carr needs to put on weight.
quotes.quote: From the JJ ESPN interview, JJ made a point to say that Carr needs to put on weight. We knew that was his answer when asked if he will be in the rotation right away. Kinda blunt. I would say I've grown less optimistic that Carr will start the season in the rotation, but I think he will eventually get there because I think the talent is too the talent and the athleticism.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' roster construction and the importance of defensive depth
quotes.excerpt: I think this group hits their ceiling, wins a championship, at least the current version of the group.
quotes.quote: I think this group hits their ceiling, wins a championship, at least the current version of the group. In my opinion, it's not going to be because they're more talented, because I think there are teams that objectively have more talent on paper than the Lakers do. It's going to be because this group is greater than the sum of their parts together. And it's going to be Luka is the best player in the world and Austin grows into being an awesome number two and Walker Kessler actually actualizes his potential as that Rudy Gobert type force, but I think a higher offensive ceiling. Quentin Grimes gets back to being who he was a few years ago, shoots the ball really well. Zaire pops, Mamu pops, Matisse, etcetera. Like, like these things collectively happen that help the Lakers hit their ceiling and offset maybe on paper not having the same top-end talent as some of these other teams or or maybe like mid-tier talent.
